To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

HPS-5 is an autosomal recessive disorder of lysosome biogenesis resulting in a deficiency of the BLOC-2 protein HPS5 and the ultrastructural findings of HPS5-deficiency resemble those of HPS3, a deficiency of another BLOC-2 subunit.

HPS-5 is a disorder of melanosome biogenesis that results in a mistrafficking of melanocyte-specific enzymes, tyrosinase and tyrosinase-related protein 1, which are normally transported in vesicles to the melanosomes.
HPS-5 patients have a distinct ultrastructural phenotype of their melanocytes, and that the trafficking of melanocyte proteins is disrupted in HPS- 5 melanocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the trafficking of TYRP1 and tyrosinase in HPS-3 and HPS-5, two distinct types of HPS that have similar ultrastructural defects in their melanocytes.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the formation of melanosomes in HPS-3 and HPS-5 patients and the trafficking of melanosome proteins in the absence of the HPS proteins.
the trafficking of proteins involved in melanosome biogenesis and the role of the BLOC-2 protein HPS5 in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BLOC-2 is required for the trafficking of melanosome proteins to the melanosomes.
the trafficking of TYRP1 and tyrosinase is defective in HPS- 5 melanocytes, but that the trafficking of Pmel17 is preserved.
HPS5 is a component of the TYRP1 trafficking machinery in melanocytes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HPS5 is required for the efficient trafficking of tyrosinase and possibly TYRP1 to melanosomes.
HPS-5 deficiency causes a mistrafficking of melanocyte-specific organelles.
HPS-5 is a component of BLOC-2 that functions in the trafficking of tyrosinase and/or TYRP1, but not Pmel17.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the trafficking of melanosome components is disrupted in HPS-2, -3, and -5, and that the BLOC-2 complex plays an important role in the trafficking of tyrosinase and tyrosinase-related protein 1 to melanosomes.
HPS-3 and HPS-5 have similar phenotypes, but HPS-3 cells have more severe melanosomal defects.
BLOC-2 is essential for trafficking of melanocyte proteins to melanosomes, but not for melanosome formation.
